To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the electric form factor of the octet of baryons has been calculated from the lattice at six values of Q in a range from 0.2 to 1.3 Gev, 2. the lattice results have been extrapolated to the experimentally measured values of the pseudoscalar masses using a formalism inspired from chiral perturbation, 3. the results of this extrapolation agree well with experiment for the proton, 4. the ratio μp
the electric form factors are consistent with the experimental results for the physical pion mass and the magnetic moment of the proton, which is consistent with the most recent experimental results.

the lattice QCD results for the electric and magnetic form factors of the baryons are consistent with experimental results and that the ratio of electric to magnetic form factors decreases with momentum transfer in a manner qualitatively consistent recent experimental results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the nucleon electric form factors in lattice QCD, and their comparison with the experimental data.
the calculation of the electromagnetic form factors of the light octet baryones, and their chiral extrapolation to the physical point.
the study of the nucleon structure using lattice QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electric form factors obtained from lattice simulations are consistent with experiment and the theoretical uncertainties are under control.

lattice QCD calculations of the electric form factors are in good agreement with experiment, but that there are some indications that lattice results for the ratio μp G p E/G pM are somewhat larger than the experimental values.
the lattice results for the electric and magnetic form factors, and for the ratios of electric and magnetic form factor ratios, are consistent with the experimental results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

lattice QCD results for the electric and magnetic form factors of the baryon octet, when extrapolated to physical pion masses, are consistent with experiment and provide a valuable test of chiral extrapolation methods.
the electric form factors obtained from lattice QCD agree very well with experiment at physical quark masses, while the ratio μp/GpM shows some tension with experiment.
the electric form factors calculated on the lattice agree with the experimental data and the magnetic form factors calculated on lattice agree with the magnetic form factors from experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lattice data for the electric form factor of the nucleon, and the other octet baryonic form factors, are of sufficiently high quality that they can be used to make reliable predictions for the form factors at the physical pseudoscalars masses.

the formalism we use is a useful tool for analyzing lattice results, as it provides a simple and accurate method for performing the necessary chiral extrapolation of the lattice results to the physical pion mass.
the electric and magnetic form factors are well described by chiral effective theory with finite-range regularized pion exchange.
